paragraphs: Mentioned in [Bava Kamma 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.99b.23). According to [Rashi’s explanation](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bava_Kamma.99b.23.1), he and Danko were money changers. Were it not for Rashi's explanation, it would be plausible to read these as names of coins, danka and issar. See Dikdukei Soferim.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman’s alternative coin-name interpretation is explicitly counterfactual: it would be plausible were it not for Rashi’s explanation of two money changers.

Hyman cites 49b. The link opens 99b, where Rav Pappa uses Dankhu and Isur as examples of expert money changers. Rashi spells the first name Dankhi and explicitly calls them both professional money changers. Hyman retains the coin-name possibility as a counterfactual.
